active_case.statement_note: Ideal proximal chain under the log-concave, log-smooth setting recorded by SampleWiki.
source_proof_route: Run the forward and backward heat-flow interpolation associated with one ideal proximal step.
Use KL/Fisher dissipation along the simultaneous heat flows.
Use displacement convexity of KL and the slope/transport inequality to control the Fisher term by Wasserstein distance.
Use Cauchy--Schwarz and Wasserstein contraction to obtain one-step reciprocal-KL growth.
Telescope the reciprocal inequality over n ideal steps and invert it.
open_interfaces: Relative Fisher-information interface for the forward/backward heat flows.
Wasserstein contraction and time-reversal glue needed to discharge the one-step reciprocal inequality.
